messages.author: cb25d91fd630a4e5
messages.subject: Plotting logit-transformed binomial data fails
parts:
The code below first fits a smoother to binomial data then transforms
the y-axis to logit scale, which should linearize the smooth.
Unfortunately the plot completely fails. Any ideas why?

data("kyphosis", package="rpart")
kyphosis$y = as.numeric(kyphosis$Kyphosis)-1
ggplot(
data = kyphosis
, mapping = aes(
x = Age
, y = y
)
)+
layer(
stat = 'smooth'
, stat_params = list(
method="glm"
, family="binomial"
)
)+
coord_trans(y='logit')


--
Mike Lawrence

Department of Psychology
Dalhousie University

This helps to show the problem:

kyphosis$y = as.numeric(kyphosis$Kyphosis)-1
ggplot(kyphosis, aes(Age, y)) +
geom_point() +
stat_smooth(method = "glm", family = "binomial")

There are data points at 0 and 1, which become -Inf and Inf under the
logistic transformation.

Hadley

> But the documentation states that the transformation happens at the

Correct.

> In that case the smoothed values that I'm
> actually plotting do not contain 1 or 0.
Also correct.

> Furthermore, I should be
> able to grab the result of the smooth and plot just that (..y.. it
> seems from the documentation).

Unfortunately it's not that simple. This is pretty subtle and took me
a while to get right, but the scales have to be trained with the raw
data as well as the output of the statistics - this is what enables
(among other things) fullrange = T to work for stat_smooth.

Hadley

messages.author: 262bfcbf6d4ecc3a
messages.subject: Re: Plotting logit-transformed binomial data fails
parts:
So, the short answer is that it's not possible to do the transform on
a value derived from raw data if the transform cannot be applied to
the raw data as well. So... back to getting predicted values
beforehand and plotting them. Unfortunately I lose the nice 95%CI
ribbon.

simple modification to your example. would be...

kyphosis$y = as.numeric(kyphosis$Kyphosis)-1
ggplot(kyphosis, aes(Age, y)) + geom_point() +

+ stat_smooth(aes(y=..y..), method = "glm", family = "binomial")
